glyph_origin: Oracle bone script: Pictogram (象形): a jade artifact with carved patterns. Original form of 彫 (“to carve”). The character was later borrowed as a country name and 口 was added as a distinguishing mark. A semi-conservative version in which the carvings are visible is 𠕛. The top part of the character gradually became similar to 用 in the late Western Zhou period. See also 黃, which could have a reference to a jade artifact. Folk etymology interprets the seal script form as 口 (“mouth”) + 用 (“to use”), indicating the idea of using words skillfully to express oneself, thereby implying the meaning of being meticulous or detailed.
